questions.stem: What is a Traditional Data Stack (TDS)?
options: A set of cloud-native analytics tools
A collection of spreadsheets used before databases existed
A stack of backup tapes kept off site
An on-premises solution that can include any kind of database or a Hadoop environment
A single relational database with no other components
questions.explanation: TDS is the on-premises solution, which can include any kind of database or even a Hadoop environment.

questions.stem: What is a Modern Data Stack (MDS)?
options: The newest version of an on-premises database
The tools and technologies that run on the Cloud
A Hadoop cluster installed in a company's own data centre
A stack of servers bought in the last two years
A data warehouse with a new user interface
questions.explanation: MDS refers to the tools and technologies on the Cloud, in contrast to the on-premises TDS.

questions.stem: The comparison of Modern Data Stack versus Traditional Data Stack is essentially a comparison of what?
options: Cloud versus on-premises infrastructures
Relational versus NoSQL databases
Batch versus streaming data
Structured versus unstructured data
Open source versus commercial software
questions.explanation: MDS versus TDS is more a comparison between Cloud and on-premises infrastructures.

questions.stem: In a Traditional Data Stack, what is involved when new hardware is needed?
options: A few clicks in a web console
A software licence renewal
A change to the database schema
Nothing; hardware scales automatically
A complete procurement cycle
questions.explanation: In TDS or on-premises environments, needing new hardware means going through a complete procurement cycle.

questions.stem: In the Traditional Data Stack CPU example, a business needs 2 CPUs at night and 4 CPUs in the daytime. What does it end up paying for?
options: 2 CPUs for 24 hours
4 CPUs only during the day
4 CPUs for 24 hours, because the hardware has already been bought
6 CPUs shared across two servers
Only the hours the CPUs are actually busy
questions.explanation: On premises you have already bought the hardware, so you pay for 4 CPUs around the clock even though only 2 are needed at night.

questions.stem: How far away is any resource when working in a Modern Data Stack on the Cloud?
options: A full procurement cycle away
A few clicks away
A hardware delivery away
A data centre visit away
A budget approval away
questions.explanation: In MDS, when you are on the Cloud, any resource is only a few clicks away.

questions.stem: In the Modern Data Stack CPU example, how does payment work for 2 CPUs at night and 4 in the daytime?
options: You pay for 4 CPUs for 24 hours
You pay a flat monthly fee regardless of usage
You pay for 6 CPUs to cover both periods
You only pay for the CPUs while you are using them
You pay for the night CPUs but the day CPUs are free
questions.explanation: On the Cloud you only pay for the 2 CPUs at night while using them, and the same applies to the daytime CPU requirement.

questions.stem: Which environment is mentioned as something a Traditional Data Stack may include besides databases?
options: A Hadoop environment
A cloud object store
A serverless function platform
A software-as-a-service analytics suite
A managed data lakehouse
questions.explanation: TDS is the on-premises solution, which can include any kind of database or a Hadoop environment as well.

questions.stem: Which statement about the Traditional Data Stack is NOT true?
options: It is an on-premises solution
It can include any kind of database
New hardware requires a procurement cycle
You pay for purchased hardware whether or not it is fully used
Any resource is a few clicks away
questions.explanation: Having resources a few clicks away is a characteristic of the Modern Data Stack on the Cloud, not of the on-premises Traditional Data Stack.

questions.stem: What is suggested as the first step to understanding the Modern Data Stack easily?
options: Learning a cloud vendor's pricing model
Migrating a database to the cloud
First understanding the Traditional Data Stack
Reading the Hype Cycle for Data Management
Building a Hadoop cluster
questions.explanation: To make MDS easy to understand, one must first understand the Traditional Data Stack (TDS).
